phase: Visible-only independent fidelity and complete-option mathematics; still before manifest, draft key/intent/report and answer candidate
method: For each question, task_fidelity/redundancy/answer_leakage were considered first, and then mathematics was solved without author keys. Symbolic formula alternatives assert general identities over the stated domain, not an accidental equality at one special parameter. Every option is assessed as an entire conjunction when it contains several results.

task_fidelity.evidence: Tests the three written section relationships: axial, base-parallel, and apex-plane. C says an interior slice; E distinguishes a real chord from B's overbroad all-apex-plane claim. Positive dimensions and solid-intersection convention are explicit adaptations. No construction output is observed, but the shape distinctions and degeneration judgment remain.

redundancy.evidence: A tests the axial special case, C tests similarity/parallel slicing, and B,D,E test the quantifier and equal generators for off-axis cuts. B and E are not duplicates: one includes supporting/exterior planes and the other requires a nonzero chord.

answer_leakage.evidence: The stem defines a section without naming its shapes. Options do not repeat a stem-given solution, and no other question states its A/C/E truth set.

mathematics.independent_solution: Axial section has two equal slants and a diameter base; an interior parallel section is a disk; any apex plane cutting a positive-length base chord has two equal generators and is isosceles. A supporting apex plane may intersect in only one generator, and some apex planes intersect only at the apex. Full true set A,C,E.

option_checks.evidence: Both apex-to-diameter endpoints are generators of equal length l, so the axial triangle is isosceles.

A tangent plane through a generator meets the solid in that line segment, not a triangle; the base-parallel plane at the apex gives a point. One explicit counterexample refutes 'as long as through apex'.
An interior parallel slice is a homothetic copy of the positive-radius filled base, so a disk; its strictly interior condition excludes the apex-point degeneration.
Even off-axis, the two boundary generators both have length l; a nonzero chord therefore gives an isosceles, not a scalene, triangle.
A positive chord makes the section nondegenerate and its apex-to-endpoint edges are equal generators, irrespective of whether the plane contains the axis.

option_checks.evidence: The unique apex would have to be the inversion center, but the inverted base lies outside the one-sided finite cone; hence no center.
Rotational symmetry of the base is not infinitely many spatial axes; only the apex-to-center line works, and all planes through it, not just one, are mirror planes.
Exactly no center, one spatial axis, and infinitely many axial mirror planes for any positive-height/radius finite right cone.
Rotating any one axial mirror plane through any angle gives another mirror plane, so there are infinitely many, not two.

phi=90 makes d=0, half chord R and altitude h, giving R*h=R^2*tan(alpha).
phi=alpha makes d=R and chord length zero. Area is zero, not the positive R^2/cos(alpha), and the section is not a triangle.
